stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Share of Varnhold Speakers Producing the Vowel Merger

| Age group | 2004 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| 18–30 | 41% | 78% |
| 31–50 | 33% | 59% |
| 51–70 | 22% | 36% |
| 71 and older | 15% | 19% |

Linguist Teodora Vasić studies a vowel merger in the coastal town of Varnhold, where word pairs such as ‘pail’ and ‘pell’ have begun to sound identical. She interviewed residents in 2004 and again in 2024, recording the share of speakers in each age group who pronounced the pairs the same way. The merger spread fastest among younger residents, but it also advanced among middle-aged speakers: in 2024, the share of speakers aged 31–50 who produced the merger was ______
explanation: The statement names two things: the 31–50 row and the 2024 column. Where they cross, the table shows 59%, so that is the value that completes the statement.

A.why: You found the right row but read the 2004 column. The statement asks about 2024.

C.why: You read the 2024 column, but your eye slipped one row down to the 51–70 group.

D.why: You read the 2024 column, but your eye slipped one row up to the 18–30 group, which the passage mentions just before the blank.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Results of Winter Cover Crop Trial

| Winter treatment | Nitrogen retained (kg per hectare) | Weed biomass (g per square meter) |
|---|---|---|
| Crimson clover | 46 | 112 |
| Cereal rye | 71 | 58 |
| Hairy vetch | 52 | 97 |
| No cover crop | 18 | 205 |

Agronomists at a research farm compared four winter treatments to see how well each kept nitrogen in the soil until spring planting. Nitrogen that plant roots do not hold can wash out of fields during winter rains, so a cover crop that retains more of it may reduce the need for fertilizer. The two legumes did less well than cereal rye on this measure but still outperformed bare ground: plots planted with hairy vetch retained ______ of nitrogen per hectare.
explanation: Find the hairy vetch row and read the nitrogen column. The cell shows 52 kilograms per hectare.

A.why: 71 kilograms is the value for cereal rye, the row just above hairy vetch, not for hairy vetch.

B.why: 97 is in the hairy vetch row, but it comes from the weed biomass column, in grams per square meter. It does not measure nitrogen.

D.why: 46 kilograms is the value for crimson clover, the other legume. You read the wrong row.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
P-Wave Arrivals Following the Calder Basin Earthquake

| Station | Distance from epicenter (km) | P-wave arrival (seconds after onset) |
|---|---|---|
| Kelso Ridge | 48 | 8.1 |
| Marrow Flat | 95 | 15.9 |
| Dunlow | 140 | 23.4 |
| Ost Harbor | 212 | 34.7 |

When an earthquake occurs, the fastest seismic waves, called P waves, travel outward from the source and reach nearby monitoring stations first. By comparing arrival times across a network of stations, seismologists can find where a quake began. After a moderate earthquake beneath the Calder Basin, researchers compiled readings from four stations at increasing distances from the epicenter. Their records show that the P waves reached the Dunlow station ______ after the earthquake began.
explanation: Find the Dunlow row and read the arrival-time column. The cell shows 23.4 seconds.

B.why: 140 is in the Dunlow row, but it is the station's distance from the epicenter in kilometers, not an arrival time.

C.why: 34.7 seconds is the arrival time at Ost Harbor, one row below Dunlow.

D.why: 15.9 seconds is the arrival time at Marrow Flat, one row above Dunlow.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Days with Morning Fog at Pell County Regional Airport

| Month | 2021–22 season | 2022–23 season |
|---|---|---|
| October | 9 | 14 |
| November | 13 | 11 |
| December | 11 | 16 |
| January | 7 | 10 |

Radiation fog forms on clear, calm nights, when the ground loses heat quickly and cools the air just above it to its dew point. Meteorologists at a regional airport counted the days with morning fog in four months of the cold season over two consecutive seasons. Their records show that in the 2021–22 season, the month with the greatest number of fog days at the airport was ______
explanation: Look only at the 2021–22 column: 9, 13, 11 and 7. The largest value, 13, is in the November row.

A.why: October had 9 fog days in 2021–22, fewer than November and December.

C.why: December has the highest count in the table overall, 16, but that number is in the 2022–23 column. The statement asks about 2021–22.

D.why: January had the fewest fog days in 2021–22, not the most. You reversed the direction the statement asks for.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Recorded Variants of ‘The Miller’s Three Sons’ in the Esk Region

| District | Variants recorded | Variants with a talking-animal helper |
|---|---|---|
| Northern uplands | 34 | 21 |
| River valley | 27 | 9 |
| Coastal plain | 41 | 30 |
| Island districts | 18 | 12 |

Folklorists often trace how a single story changes as it passes from teller to teller. From 2015 to 2019, folklorist Maren Holt recorded spoken versions of ‘The Miller’s Three Sons,’ a tale told throughout the Esk region. For each version, she noted whether a talking animal helps the youngest son. Holt found that the tale was told more often in some districts than in others; in the river valley, she recorded ______ variants of the tale.
explanation: The statement asks for the total number of variants recorded in the river valley. In the river valley row, the ‘Variants recorded’ column shows 27.

A.why: 9 is in the river valley row, but it counts only the variants with a talking-animal helper, not all the variants Holt recorded.

B.why: 34 is the count for the northern uplands, one row above the river valley.

C.why: 41 is the count for the coastal plain, one row below the river valley.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Average Insect Visits per Hour to Four Wildflower Species

| Species | Meadow | Roadside verge |
|---|---|---|
| Oxeye daisy | 14 | 9 |
| Bird’s-foot trefoil | 22 | 17 |
| Wild carrot | 11 | 15 |
| Field scabious | 19 | 6 |

Ecologists counted the insect visits that four wildflower species received in an unmowed meadow and along a nearby roadside verge. The plots were matched in size, sun exposure and flower density, so differences in visits could be attributed mainly to habitat. Some species drew far fewer pollinators beside the road. On roadside verges, for example, field scabious received an average of ______ visits per hour.
explanation: Find the field scabious row and read the roadside verge column. The cell shows 6 visits per hour.

B.why: 9 is the roadside value for oxeye daisy, the first row, not for field scabious.

C.why: 15 is the roadside value for wild carrot, the row directly above field scabious.

D.why: 19 is in the field scabious row, but it comes from the meadow column. The statement asks about roadside verges.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Accuracy of Successive Harlan Valley Survey Maps

| Edition | Year published | Mean positional error (meters) |
|---|---|---|
| First | 1872 | 140 |
| Second | 1911 | 85 |
| Third | 1954 | 31 |
| Fourth | 1998 | 4 |

Cartographers judge a map’s accuracy by comparing where features appear on the map with where they actually lie on the ground. A study of four successive editions of a regional survey map of the Harlan Valley found that accuracy improved sharply as surveying tools advanced, from chains and compasses to aerial photography and satellite positioning. The researchers report that the mean positional error of the third edition, published in 1954, was ______
explanation: Find the third edition row (1954) and read the error column. The cell shows 31 meters.

A.why: 4 meters is the error for the fourth edition, published in 1998, one row below the third.

B.why: 85 meters is the error for the second edition, published in 1911, one row above the third.

C.why: 140 meters is the error for the first edition. It is the most memorable number in the column, but it belongs to the wrong row.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Artifacts Recovered from the Main Trench at Tell Varo

| Layer | Approximate date | Pottery sherds | Stone tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layer 1 (top) | 900 CE | 312 | 18 |
| Layer 2 | 600 CE | 247 | 46 |
| Layer 3 | 300 CE | 158 | 83 |
| Layer 4 (bottom) | 1 CE | 64 | 129 |

At Tell Varo, excavators divided their main trench into four layers, each from a different period of occupation. Pottery fragments are more common in the upper, more recent layers, and stone tools are more common in the deeper, older ones. Archaeologist Idris Sallam concluded that over time the community came to rely more on pottery and less on stone tools. As one piece of support, Sallam notes that layer 3 yielded ______ stone tools.
explanation: Find the layer 3 row and read the stone tools column. The cell shows 83.

A.why: 46 is the stone tool count for layer 2, one row above layer 3.

B.why: 129 is the stone tool count for layer 4, the bottom layer, one row below layer 3.

D.why: 158 is in the layer 3 row, but it is the number of pottery sherds, not stone tools.
